speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me more about the swelling and pain in your right ring finger, specifically when it started and if there was any recent injury or bite?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail. Is the swelling localized to the joint or the entire finger, and are you able to fully straighten and bend the finger without significant pain or mechanical catching?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Those symptoms strongly suggest a mallet finger injury, where the tendon is torn or avulsed at the distal interphalangeal joint. I will now order an X-ray to check for any associated bony avulsion fracture.

REQUEST TEST: X-Ray_Right_Hand

speaker: Doctor
text:
The X-ray confirms no fracture, which points to a pure tendon injury. Since the clinical signs are classic for a mallet finger with an intact extensor tendon mechanism otherwise, I am confident in the diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet finger (extensor tendon avulsion/rupture)

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
